title: The Devout Israelite
logline: A poor spinner gives his whole day's earnings to a friend in need, trades his last two worthless things for a rotten fish, finds a pearl inside it, and when he is rich gives half away again at his own door, to a stranger who turns out to be a messenger sent to test him.
moral: True generosity does not depend on how much you have: he gave when he was poor and he gave when he was rich.
tone: Warm, plain and gentle, with one comic stretch (the stinking fish and the swap), one burst of wonder (the pearl) and a quiet, luminous ending. The humour is never at the hero's expense.

beats.summary: A good man and his family live from day to day by spinning cotton.
The routine: sell thread, buy cotton and just enough food. Coins end at zero every day.
A friend in desperate need stops him in the market.
He gives the friend every coin he earned.
He comes home with no food and no cotton.
Only a cracked platter and an old jar are left to sell.
Nobody in the market wants them.
A fish seller is stuck with one swollen, stinking fish.
The two men swap their unwanted goods.
Inside the fish the family finds a large pearl.
The pearl has never been drilled.
The expert says it is very valuable and sends him to a richer buyer.
At his own door a poor man asks for alms.
He splits the fortune in two and offers half without hesitation.
The poor man gives it back.
He is a messenger sent to test the man's generosity.
The man has passed the test.
Wealth did not change him: he is still ready to give.

sets.description: The family hut in cutaway (walls x 110..890, floor y 900): stool, mat, shelf with the platter and jar, peg with the purse, window onto the live sky. Poor state for S1-S15; comfortable state in S27 (carpet, lit lamp, full shelf, food tray) dressed by the scene.

Outside the home: cottage with an opening door at the right edge, trees, keyed sun or time of day. Family seen in the doorway through the inside callback. Used at dawn (S5), dusk (S7) and afternoon (S13, S19-S26, S28).

A 1600-wide street strip: cloth stall at x 380, cotton sacks (props) at x 800, food stall at x 1200 (S3 anchors, approximate, take from the returned stalls anchors), palace false. For S11-S12 an empty stall at about x 1000 dressed as the fish stall (plank counter, one fish, palm-leaf fan).
palaceHall variant 'merchant' in its modest dressing: ochre wall, shelves, low desk with a gem tray and a small coin stack, curtain closed, window at morning (u 0.12).
The same merchant hall dressed rich: wall 'blue', curtain open on the treasure alcove, carpet, taller coin stacks on the desk, one stool at the left for the hero to drop onto.

props.description: Drop spindle, distaff with cotton, cotton basket and thread skeins (see new_assets).
Cracked wooden platter and old clay jar (see new_assets).
The planned Library fish (KD-007, KD-019) in palette 2 (round, pink), used as a dead market fish: roll, limp, eyes x, puff; plus a new open field (see new_assets).
The planned pearl (AN-088 pearlSack + pearl): r 14 small, r 26 in the hand, r 60 for the S15 insert with a sliding highlight.

Planned coinPile (single coins and small stacks), planned sack with a coin mark (the fortune: three sacks in S18-S19, shown as four equal sacks from S22 so that half reads), planned purse (empty on the peg, limp in the friend's hand, small gift in S28).
Planned brass tray with bread and dates: the daily food in S3-S4, empty in S8, full in S27-S28.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل صالح من بني إسرائيل|يعيش مع أسرته من غزل القطن.|كانت أسرته تغزل الخيوط كل يوم، فيبيعها،|ثم يشتري قطنًا جديدًا وطعامًا بما يبقى من المال ليكفيهم يومهم.
subtitles.en: A devout Israelite|supported his family by selling the cotton thread they spun.|He used the proceeds|to buy more cotton and enough food for the day.

subtitles.ar: وفي صباح خرج الرجل ليبيع الخيوط كما اعتاد.|قابله صديق يشكو الفقر والحاجة،|فتأثر بحاله وأعطاه كل ما قبضه من ثمن الغزل،|ثم رجع إلى البيت دون طعام أو قطن.
subtitles.en: One morning|a friend complained of desperate need.|The man gave him all the money from that day’s thread|and returned home without food or fresh cotton.

subtitles.ar: سألته أسرته عما حدث،|فأخبرهم أنه ساعد رجلًا محتاجًا.|لم يبق في البيت شيء يمكن بيعه إلا طبق خشبي متشقق وجرة قديمة،|فأخذهما إلى السوق، لكن أحدًا لم يرغب فيهما.
subtitles.en: His family wondered|how they would eat.|Only a cracked wooden platter and an old jar remained to sell,|but nobody in the market would buy them.

subtitles.ar: رأى بائع سمك يعرض سمكة منتفخة ذات رائحة كريهة،|ولم يجد من يشتريها.|اتفق الرجلان على تبديل السلع،|فأخذ الرجل السمكة، وترك للبائع الطبق والجرة، ثم عاد إلى أسرته.
subtitles.en: A fish seller had a swollen, foul-smelling fish|that no one wanted.|They exchanged their unwanted goods,|and the man carried the fish home.

subtitles.ar: فتحت الأسرة بطن السمكة لتعدها للطعام،|فوجدت لؤلؤة كبيرة داخلها.|فحصها الرجل، ورأى أنها لم تثقب من قبل.|وفي اليوم التالي حملها إلى خبير بالأحجار الكريمة ليسأله عن قيمتها.
subtitles.en: When the family opened the fish,|they discovered a large pearl.|It had never been drilled.|The next day the man took it to a jewel expert.

subtitles.ar: قال الخبير إن اللؤلؤة ثمينة،|لكنه نصحه بزيارة تاجر يملك مالًا أكثر.|ذهب الرجل إليه، فدفع له سبعين ألف درهم مقابل اللؤلؤة،|وعاد إلى بيته يحمل ثروة لم يتوقعها.
subtitles.en: The expert|recommended a wealthier buyer.|That merchant paid seventy thousand dirhams for the pearl,|giving the family a fortune they had never imagined.

subtitles.ar: عند باب البيت قابله فقير وطلب منه صدقة.|تذكر الرجل كيف كان محتاجًا بالأمس،|فقسم المال نصفين، وقدم نصفه للفقير دون تردد، مع أن أسرته عانت الجوع منذ وقت قريب.
subtitles.en: At his door a beggar asked for help.|Remembering his own poverty,|the man immediately divided the money in half and offered the beggar one share.

subtitles.ar: لكن الفقير أعاد المال إليه،|وقال إنه رسول أرسل لاختبار كرمه، وإنه نجح في الامتحان.|شكر الرجل الله، وعاش مع أسرته في راحة،|بعدما ظل مستعدًا للعطاء حتى بعد غناه.
subtitles.en: The beggar returned the money|and revealed he was a messenger sent to test the man’s generosity.|The family lived comfortably,|and the man’s willingness to share had endured.

new_assets.name: spinningKit
new_assets.description: One module for any spinning or weaving home. spindle(ctx, x, y, {len, spin, fill}): the hanging thread is a line of length len (60..220) from the hand point (x, y); the spindle is a stick 70 long and 6 wide with a whorl disc r 14 near the bottom and a white thread cone on it that grows with fill 0..1 (up to 26 wide x 40 tall); spin is a phase that slides 3 diagonal lines across the cone and whorl. distaff(ctx, x, y, {fill}): a stick 120 long with a cotton cloud of 5 white circles r 18 (blue dot shading) whose size follows fill. cottonBasket(ctx, x, y, {fill, tip}): basket 110 x 70 (brown weave lines) with 0..6 white puffs; tip rotates it up to upside down. skein(ctx, x, y, {n}): figure-of-eight hanks 60 x 26, white with three blue lines, stacked n high.
new_assets.implementation: Flat shapes with the style brush outline: K rounded rects and circles, Ben-Day dots through the style dot fill clipped to each shape. spin is a pure function of t (phase = t * 9). The thread from distaff to hand to spindle is two straight segments redrawn each frame from the hand anchors (P.hands).

new_assets.name: platterJar
new_assets.description: Two small props in one file. platter(ctx, x, y, {r: 46, crack, tilt}): round wooden dish seen at three quarters (ellipse 92 x 60, brown with a darker rim and two grain arcs); crack 0..1 draws a 5-segment black zigzag from the rim to past the centre. oldJar(ctx, x, y, {h: 90, chip, web}): clay jar 70 wide x 90 tall (belly ellipse, 34 wide neck, rim ring, one ear handle), terracotta with red dot shading; chip removes a notch from the rim; web draws one spider thread with a dot spider that can swing. Both are drawn at about 0.9 scale in hands and on the shelf.
new_assets.implementation: Ellipses and paths with the style outline; crack is a polyline revealed by length. Check planned hangingJar and waterJug first: if one of them is already drawn, oldJar should be that function with a plain palette, chip and web options.

new_assets.name: fish
new_assets.description: The planned side-view comic fish (KD-007, KD-019), palette 2 (round, pink), about 200 x 110 on the counter. Fields used here: roll 0.5 (on its side), limp 1, eyes x, puff 0..1 (swollen: body height +35 %, belly line bulges), tail swing when carried.
new_assets.implementation: As specified by the earlier plans; this film needs only the dead, market use. If the fish is not yet in the Library, draw palette 2 first with roll, limp, puff and eyes x, and leave the swimming fields for the water films.

new_assets.name: fish open (belly flap)
new_assets.description: Opt-in field open 0..1 on the fish: a curved flap along the lower belly (about 110 long) hinges downward to 70 degrees and shows a dark navy hollow with blue dots, 90 x 44. Nothing anatomical is drawn. The hollow is the stage for the glow and the pearl.
new_assets.implementation: Clip the hollow ellipse to the body shape, fill navy with the style dots, then draw the flap as a rotated copy of the belly segment about its upper edge. Default 0 leaves the fish unchanged.

new_assets.name: pearl
new_assets.description: Planned pearl (AN-088): white disc with a pale blue crescent shadow, a small white highlight with a black outline and an optional four-point glint star; sizes r 14, r 26 and r 60. This film adds highlight angle (the highlight slides round the disc to show the pearl turning) for the S15 insert.
new_assets.implementation: Circle, crescent by clipping a second offset circle, highlight position = centre + 0.5 r at the given angle. Glint star from the style emphasis primitive or four thin triangles.

new_assets.name: stinkLines
new_assets.description: Planned smell lines with flies (AN-090): 3 to 5 green wavy vertical strokes rising about 160 units from a point, appearing one by one and drifting upward on a loop, plus 2 flies on seeded figure-of-eight loops. Strength 0..1 thins them out after the fish is opened.
new_assets.implementation: Sine-offset polylines with tapering width, phase from t; flies are 4 px dots with two wing ticks, position from K.noise seeds.

new_assets.name: goldGlow
new_assets.description: Planned treasure light (KD-031): tapering rays, a halftone disc and staggered star glints, strength 0..1. Here in a white and pale yellow palette for the pearl (S14, S18) and weak yellow for the coin sacks (S19).
new_assets.implementation: As planned; add a colour option.

new_assets.name: angelLight
new_assets.description: Planned effect (AN-075): a figure bleaches to white from the feet up (p 0..0.4), then is replaced by a tapering column of light 90 wide x 300 tall with a round glow at head height, yellow halftone rays and star glints, and shrinks to a star (p 0.4..1). In this film the wings are switched off by default (wings:false), see owner_questions. Used with the planned skyLight cone from the top of the frame.
new_assets.implementation: As planned in AN-075: redraw the person with a clip line rising from the feet and a white palette below it, then cross-fade to the column (rounded tapering path, yellow dot halo). Add the wings option.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: Planned wordless picture balloon. Three uses: the friend's need (empty bowl, thin child) at 29.9; the hero's account (coins travelling from his hand to the friend) at 46.3; the expert's advice (a big turban over a tall coin stack) at 117.9.
new_assets.implementation: As planned; contents are small calls of person heads, coinPile and a bowl ellipse.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: P3 Arabic says the family asked what had happened and he told them he had helped a needy man; the English says "His family wondered how they would eat." Both are kept verbatim; the picture follows the Arabic.

SCRIPT: P7 Arabic ends with "although his family had suffered hunger only recently", which has no English counterpart; P7 is therefore cut into 3 subtitle chunks and the last English chunk stays on screen during that clause.
SCRIPT: P8 Arabic includes "and that he had passed the test. The man thanked God", which the English omits; both kept verbatim, the picture follows the Arabic.
SCRIPT: P1 Arabic says he lived "with his family from spinning cotton" and details buying with what remained "to suffice them for the day"; the English is a looser summary. Kept verbatim.
The messenger is shown as a faceless column of light with no wings and no face after the reveal (default); the alternative is the planned angelLight with wings.
The hero wears the plain villager costume with no religious or ethnic markers; "Israelite" is carried only by the narration and subtitles (default).
Thanking God is shown as kneeling with open raised palms and eyes to the sky, with no specific ritual posture (default).
The fish is opened as a clean flap onto a dark hollow: no blood or insides (default).

Added beyond the script: in the last scene the friend from the market walks past and the hero gives to him, to show "still ready to give after he became rich" (default: keep; alternative: an anonymous passer-by).
Added beyond the script: the wife gives a small nod of approval while half the fortune is offered (default: keep), so the family is seen to share the choice rather than suffer it.
Invented lettering: SPIN!, SOLD!, ALL OF IT!, NO THANKS!, PHEW!, SWAP!, A PEARL!, 70,000!, HALF FOR YOU!, YOU PASSED!, and the transition card NEXT DAY... (default: keep all eleven).
The fortune is drawn as three sacks when paid and as four equal sacks from the dividing scene on, so that "half" reads at a glance (default); the alternative is one sack poured into two piles.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; cue every action with w(p, n) from timing.json. The cue times in this plan are the word starts in planning/inputs/timeline.md.

Sets are single calls that return anchors: use HUT/hutRoomAnchors, VYARD, MARKET and MERCHANT anchors for door, shelf, stool, stall counters and desk instead of the approximate coordinates given here (those are read from the catalogue image: measure on the set).
Human figures face the viewer (no profile): side-to-side travel uses walk() with dir; handovers use handLW/handRW world targets meeting at a midpoint about 105 units from each figure at y about 760.

The giving gesture is a setup and payoff: define GIVE once (hero handRW to the receiver's palm, eyes on the receiver's face, 10 px draw-back anticipation) and reuse it at 32.86, 146.52 and 175.18. The poor man at the door (S20) must stand in the same screen relation to the hero as the friend in S6.
Coin counter: S.counter in the top left of the panel; 3, 1, 0 in S3; 3 to 0 in S6; DIRHAMS 0 to 70,000 in S18. Hide it in every other scene.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for automatic blinks; suppress blinks (noBlink) during the held shocks at 95.0-95.9 and 162.8-163.6.
Groups never move in unison: use stagger() for the family reactions (S1, S8, S14, S23, S26, S28).
Panel-only shake is not needed anywhere in this film except a 2-frame bump when the hero sits down hard at 125.64.
The LATER card at 102.3 carries the caption NEXT DAY...; put the camera and set cut at its covered midpoint. No other time card: the returns home are carried by the dusk sky.

Sound: narration only, plus four quiet effects (master 0.6) in the real pauses only: pop 6.87, whoosh 20.6, pop 133.4, chime 178.2 (after the last word). The pearl reveal has no pause in the narration, so it gets no sound: the glow and the held stare carry it.
Lettering never covers a face: place words in the sky or wall area above heads or on the ground strip below y 950; keep to the eleven listed words.
S21 and S19 thought clouds reuse existing scene drawings at reduced scale via thoughtCloud inside(c, t); keep figures at least 110 px tall on screen.
Scenes S20 to S26 and S28 are one continuous place (the yard at the door): keep one position function per character across them so nobody jumps on the cuts.
warnings: The fish, pearl, stinkLines, goldGlow, angelLight, iconBalloon, coinPile, sack, purse and foodTray are planned assets that may not exist in Library yet; if they do not, this film has to draw them (fish, spinningKit and angelLight are the larger ones).
Only three pauses of 0.6 s or more exist (6.54-7.20, 20.12-21.12, 133.00-133.84); the pearl reveal, the swap and the 70,000 count have no room for an effect and stay silent under the voice.
The time 25.70 for the word before "اعتاد" is interpolated in the timeline; nothing is cued to it exactly.
P7 and P8 carry more Arabic than English; the English subtitle will sit unchanged for about 4.8 s at 150.9-155.6 and the picture must carry that clause (S23).
The messenger reveal is a religiously sensitive image; it is staged as light only (see owner_questions).
S6 is 13 s in one framing; the push-in at 32 and the counter keep it alive, but check it on the contact sheet.
